findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' required by ActiveModel::Serializer convention
findings.description: Every other conditional-include gate in this serializer (include_email?, include_stats?, include_card_image_badge?, include_suspend_reason?, include_user_fields?, etc.) and the plugin API (lib/plugin/instance.rb defines include_#{attr}?) follows the ActiveModel::Serializer 0.8.3 convention of naming the gate method include_<attr>? with a question mark; this new method is named include_website_name without one, so AMS never recognizes it as the gate for :website_name and the attribute is always attempted regardless of whether a website is present or the viewer is restricted.
findings.evidence: Line 153: `def include_website_name` (no '?'), contrasted with every other gate in the same file e.g. line 117 `def include_email?`, line 161 `def include_card_image_badge_id?`, line 201 `def include_stats?`; lib/plugin/instance.rb:61 confirms the framework looks up `include_#{attr}?`.
findings.suggestion: Rename the method to `include_website_name?` so ActiveModel::Serializer actually invokes it as the inclusion gate.

findings.title: website_name is not covered by the untrusted_attributes privacy gate that hides the raw website field
findings.description: The untrusted_attributes helper (lines 105-111) hides :website (along with bio_raw, bio_cooked, location, etc.) from anonymous/TL0-restricted viewers via scope.restrict_user_fields?, but the newly added :website_name attribute is not listed there and its own include_website_name gate only checks website.present?, so a restricted viewer who cannot see the raw website URL can still see the derived host name (or full host+path in same-domain cases), defeating the intent of the redaction.
findings.evidence: Lines 105-111 list untrusted_attributes without :website_name; line 153-155 `def include_website_name; website.present?; end` has no restrict_user_fields? check, unlike untrusted_attributes' own gate at line 29 `return false if scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.
findings.suggestion: Add :website_name to the untrusted_attributes list (or otherwise gate include_website_name on scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)) so the derived field is redacted whenever the source website field is.

findings.title: Hostname comparisons in website_name are case-sensitive
findings.description: website_host (parsed via URI) and discourse_host (Discourse.current_hostname) are compared with plain string equality/ends_with in all three branches without normalizing case, but domain names are case-insensitive and URI#host does not downcase; a user-entered website like http://Example.COM/user on an instance hosted at example.com would fail every equality/suffix check and incorrectly fall through to showing only the bare host instead of the full same-domain path.
findings.evidence: Line 141 `if website_host == discourse_host`, line 144 comparing split arrays, and line 149 `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` all compare raw, non-downcased strings.
findings.suggestion: Downcase both website_host and discourse_host before comparing (e.g. website_host = URI(website.to_s).host.to_s.downcase).

findings.title: website_name attribute bypasses the untrusted_attributes privacy gate that hides website
findings.description: The new website_name attribute derives from website but its include_website_name method only checks website.present?, unlike include_website? which is generated by the untrusted_attributes DSL and returns false when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true (TL0 user viewed anonymously); as a result website_name still leaks the host/path of a website value that the serializer is deliberately hiding from anonymous viewers of low-trust users.
findings.evidence: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 25-33 define untrusted_attributes so include_#{attr}? returns false if scope.restrict_user_fields?(object); :website is passed to untrusted_attributes at line 109 but :website_name is not, and the diff's include_website_name (line 153-155) is `website.present?` with no restrict_user_fields? check; lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58 defines restrict_user_fields?(user) as `user.trust_level == TrustLevel[0] && anonymous?`.
findings.suggestion: Add website_name to the untrusted_attributes list (or add an explicit restrict_user_fields? check inside include_website_name) so the derived attribute is hidden under the same conditions as website.

findings.title: elsif branch of website_name (equal-length multi-part subdomain match) has zero test coverage
findings.description: The website_name method has three branches: exact host match, an elsif for same-segment-count hosts with more than two dot-separated parts (e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com), and a fallback else. The three new specs only exercise the if branch and both outcomes of the else branch; none set up a website host and Discourse.current_hostname that both have equal segment counts greater than two, so the elsif branch's condition, and both its true/false ternary outcomes, are never executed by any test.
findings.evidence: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 144-146: elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2 ... website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? ... ; the three specs in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb (lines 77-90) use hostnames 'discourse.org'/'example.com', 'example.com'/'example.com', and 'forums.example.com'/'example.com', none of which reach this branch (the last has differing segment counts of 3 vs 2, sending it to the else branch instead).
findings.suggestion: Add two specs: one with Discourse.current_hostname 'forum.example.com' and website 'http://www.example.com/user' (equal 3-part hosts, matching parent domain) asserting the full path is exposed, and one with a mismatched parent domain (e.g. 'forum.example.com' vs website host 'www.other.com') asserting only the host is exposed.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that inverts the ternary condition on line 146, or breaks the split/join logic for multi-segment subdomains, would silently expose full URL paths (or wrongly hide them) for any site running on a subdomain like forum.example.com, with no test catching it.

findings.title: No test verifies website_name's visibility for restricted/TL0-anonymous users
findings.description: The website attribute is included in untrusted_attributes, which hides it from anonymous viewers of low-trust-level profiles, and the spec's TL0-anonymous context asserts the whole untrusted_attributes list is absent from json. The new website_name attribute is not added to that untrusted_attributes call, and the spec's local untrusted_attributes list (line 11) was not updated to include it either, so there is no test locking in whether the derived hostname should also be hidden in that scenario.
findings.evidence: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 105-111 list untrusted_attributes without :website_name; spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb line 11 defines untrusted_attributes as %i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}, omitting website_name, and the TL0-anonymous test at lines 13-15 only iterates that list.
findings.suggestion: Add website_name to the TL0-anonymous spec's expectation (and to app/serializers/user_serializer.rb's untrusted_attributes call if it is meant to be hidden like website), then assert json does not have key :website_name for a restricted user with a website set.
findings.failure_scenario: Because website is hidden for TL0 users viewed anonymously but website_name is not gated the same way, an anonymous viewer could see the hostname of a low-trust user's website even though the raw URL is suppressed — a data-exposure gap with no test to catch it if this was unintentional.

findings.title: No test for malformed/hostless website URL hitting the rescue-nil early-return path
findings.description: website_name wraps URI(website.to_s).host in a rescue nil and then returns early if website_host is nil, which is the defensive path guarding against unparseable or schemeless website values (e.g. a URI with no host component or one that raises URI::InvalidURIError). None of the three new specs exercise a website value that triggers this rescue or the nil-host early return, so this defensive branch, added specifically to keep the serializer from raising on bad input, is unverified.
findings.evidence: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb lines 138-140: website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil ... return if website_host.nil?; all three website_name specs (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb lines 77-90) set user.user_profile.website to 'http://example.com/user', a well-formed URL with a host, so website_host is never nil in any test.
findings.suggestion: Add a spec setting user.user_profile.website to a value with no host (e.g. 'not a url' or 'javascript:alert(1)') and assert json does not include the :website_name key (since include_website_name is based on website.present?, the key would be present with a nil value unless include_website_name? also checks the parsed host) or that json[:website_name] is nil, verifying the serializer does not raise.
findings.failure_scenario: If a future edit moves the rescue or removes the early nil check, a user who enters a malformed website string (which the UI does not strictly validate) would cause the profile page's JSON serialization to raise an unhandled exception, breaking the entire user page for that profile with no test to catch the regression.

findings.title: New AMS gating method `include_website_name` is missing the required `?` suffix
findings.description: Every other conditional-inclusion method in this same serializer follows the ActiveModel::Serializer 0.8.3 convention `include_<attr>?` (with a trailing question mark) so that the serializer framework recognizes and calls it to decide whether to include the attribute; the new method is named `include_website_name` without the `?`, so AMS will not find/invoke it via its `include_#{name}?` lookup and `website_name` will always be serialized regardless of whether a website is present, unlike every sibling attribute.
findings.evidence: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb defines include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, include_suspended_till?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_card_image_badge?, include_private_message_stats?, include_edit_history_public?, include_user_fields?, and include_topic_post_count? — all ending in '?' — while the new method at line 153 is `def include_website_name` (no '?'), diverging from every other gating method in the file including the macro-generated ones (self.staff_attributes/private_attributes/untrusted_attributes at lines 6-33 which programmatically define `include_#{attr}?`).
findings.suggestion: Rename the method to `include_website_name?` so ActiveModel::Serializer's `include_#{name}?` lookup actually finds it and gates the attribute on `website.present?` as intended.

findings.title: Website host compared to instance hostname without case normalization, unlike the codebase's existing host-comparison pattern
findings.description: The new `website_name` method compares `URI(website.to_s).host` directly against `Discourse.current_hostname` (and does substring/subdomain checks on the raw split segments) without downcasing either side, whereas the codebase's existing precedent for extracting and using a URI host, `Email::Sender.host_for` in lib/email/sender.rb, explicitly downcases the host and has a dedicated spec enforcing it. Since URI#host preserves the original casing of the input URL, a user-entered website like 'http://ExamPLE.com' on an instance whose current_hostname is 'example.com' would fail the equality/subdomain checks here and be misclassified as a different domain.
findings.evidence: lib/email/sender.rb:153 `host = uri.host.downcase if uri.host.present?` with spec/components/email/sender_spec.rb:43 `it "downcases hosts" do ... expect(Email::Sender.host_for("http://ForumSite.com")).to eq("forumsite.com")`; the new app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138-149 code performs `website_host == discourse_host` and `.split('.')` comparisons with no `.downcase` anywhere in the new method.
findings.suggestion: Downcase both `website_host` and `discourse_host` (or at least website_host) before any equality/subdomain comparison, matching the established host-normalization pattern used in lib/email/sender.rb.

findings.title: include_website_name lacks the '?' suffix AMS requires, so the inclusion guard never runs and also skips the untrusted-user visibility rule applied to the sibling `website` attribute
findings.description: Encapsulation: 5/10, Expression: 2/10, Usefulness: 7/10, Enforcement: 1/10. UserSerializer's attribute-inclusion contract is enforced purely by a naming convention -- every other gating method in the file (include_email?, include_stats?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_suspend_reason?, etc.) ends in '?', which is what ActiveModel::Serializer 0.8.3 looks up via respond_to?("include_#{name}?"). The new include_website_name method omits the '?', so it is never invoked by the framework: website_name is unconditionally serialized (as null) even when website is blank, and -- unlike website itself -- it is absent from the untrusted_attributes list (line 105-111) that hides fields from TL0 users viewed anonymously, so it bypasses that visibility restriction entirely. Nothing in the type structure catches this; only a naming convention does, and the convention was violated silently.
findings.evidence: Line 153: 'def include_website_name' (missing '?') versus every sibling gate in the same file, e.g. line 117 'def include_email?', line 223 'def include_suspend_reason?', and the untrusted_attributes list at lines 105-111 which lists :website but not :website_name.
findings.suggestion: Rename to include_website_name? so AMS actually calls it, and add :website_name to the untrusted_attributes list (or otherwise mirror website's visibility gating) so the two attributes cannot diverge; ideally express the pairing structurally (e.g. derive website_name's inclusion from include_website? directly) rather than duplicating the presence check.
findings.invalid_state_example: A TL0 user viewed anonymously has website hidden (excluded per untrusted_attributes) but website_name is still present in the serialized JSON, exposing the derived hostname/path that the surrounding restriction was meant to hide.

findings.title: website_name repeats URI(website.to_s) parsing and the same concatenation expression three times
findings.description: The new website_name method parses website.to_s with URI(...) four separate times (once for .host, three times for .path in each branch) and repeats the identical website_host + URI(website.to_s).path expression in all three branches. Extracting the path and the combined full-path string into local variables once at the top removes the repeated parsing/concatenation and makes the three branches read as pure selection logic instead of re-deriving the same value each time.
findings.evidence: Lines 138-150: website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil; then URI(website.to_s).path is called again on lines 143, 146 and 149, each time re-parsing website.to_s and re-concatenating website_host + URI(website.to_s).path.
findings.suggestion: Before: website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil; ... website_host + URI(website.to_s).path (repeated in all three branches). After: website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil; return if website_host.nil?; full_website = website_host + URI(website.to_s).path; discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname; then reference full_website in each branch instead of re-deriving it.
findings.behavior_preserved: Yes — website and website.to_s do not change during the method call, so caching the parsed path and the concatenated string produces identical output to re-parsing it three times.

findings.title: website_host.split('.') and discourse_host.split('.') are each computed twice in the same branch
findings.description: In the elsif branch, website_host.split('.').length is computed on line 144 and website_host.split('.')[1..-1] is computed again on line 146; the same duplication happens for discourse_host.split('.'). Naming the split results once (e.g. website_parts, discourse_parts) and reusing them for both the length check and the suffix comparison would make the branch easier to scan without re-splitting the same string twice.
findings.evidence: Line 144: (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2 — three separate split('.') calls on the same two strings, followed by two more split('.') calls on line 146.
findings.suggestion: Before: computing website_host.split('.') and discourse_host.split('.') independently on lines 144 and 146. After: website_parts = website_host.split('.'); discourse_parts = discourse_host.split('.') once near the top of the elsif branch (or method), then use website_parts.length, discourse_parts.length, website_parts[1..-1].join('.'), discourse_parts[1..-1].join('.').
findings.behavior_preserved: Yes — split('.') is a pure function of the unchanged host strings, so caching the result changes nothing observable.
